title: Death for Striking a Man Fatally
kjv_text: He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.
summary: Fatal assault is a capital offense — the apodictic baseline that vv.13-14 immediately grade by intent.
original_audience: Israelite community; enforcement ran through the avenger of blood and local elders.
immediate_context: Opens the Covenant Code's violence section; the Decalogue's sixth commandment given teeth.
historical_context: Capital homicide law is ANE-universal; Israel's marks are the refusal of ransom (Num 35:31) and the intent distinction that follows. 'Surely be put to death' (mot yumat) is the code's recurring capital formula — it will be attached to acts modern readers find wildly unequal.
exceptions: Unintentional killing diverts to refuge (v.13); the ox-goring vicarious case allows ransom (v.30).
nt_passages: Matthew 5:38-39 — turn the other cheek, the antithesis to the code's whole method
John 8:7 — 'he that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone'

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God approve of capital punishment? Mandated here vs. Cain's protection (Gen 4:15), 'vengeance is mine' (Rom 12:19), and John 8.

usofc_implementation: USC-C Title IV's first section: murder carries mandatory death, no plea to lesser, no ransom (Num 35:31 construed as banning commutation-for-payment, i.e., banning the one corruption the courts would otherwise sell). Executions are public, scheduled between festivals, and attendance counts toward NDS devotion quotas.
constitutional_analogue: Mandatory capital sentencing — struck down in Woodson v. North Carolina (1976), restored here with liturgy.
scene_ideas: A jury that knows conviction means death and no judge can soften it, discovering nullification one juror at a time.
The festival scheduler negotiating with the execution calendar office over a date conflict.
satirical_uses: Attendance at executions earns the same devotion credit as attendance at communion; the line is shorter at communion.
